claims.text: Kodiak AI published its release naming Dallas to Houston as its driverless launch lane on September 25th, 2026.
claims.quote:
End-to-End Deliveries

September 25, 2026
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak announced plans to begin unsupervised long-haul driverless service on the Dallas-Houston freight lane by the end of 2026.
claims.quote: plans to launch unsupervised long-haul driverless service on the Dallas-Houston freight lane by the end of 2026
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says its first driverless long-haul lane will link the Dallas-Fort Worth and Houston metro areas along Interstate 45. The company puts the two areas 219 miles apart.
claims.quote: Kodiak’s first driverless long-haul lane will connect the Dallas–Fort Worth and Houston metropolitan areas, 219 miles apart along Interstate 45
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak's September 25th, 2026 release says the company began its driverless long-haul launch program in August.
claims.quote: Kodiak began its driverless long-haul launch program in August
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says it now consistently completes deliveries without human intervention between its hub in Lancaster, Texas and its Houston launch destination.
claims.quote: now consistently completes deliveries between its Lancaster, Texas, hub and its launch destination in Houston without human intervention
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says the safety observer never touched the wheel during these end-to-end deliveries, surface streets included.
claims.quote: the safety observer never touched the wheel, including on surface streets
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says its Autonomy Readiness Measure for the long-haul domain stood at 93 percent as of the end of August.
claims.quote: As of the end of August, Kodiak’s Autonomy Readiness Measure (ARM) for the long-haul domain stood at 93%
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak defines its readiness measure as the share of claims and evidence in its driverless safety case that are materially complete.
claims.quote: The ARM measures the percentage of claims and evidence in Kodiak’s safety case for driverless operations that are materially complete
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says it expects the measure to reach 100 percent and to launch driverless operations by year end.
claims.quote: The company expects to reach 100% and launch driverless operations by year end.
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak describes its safety case as a structured argument backed by evidence that its autonomous driving system can operate safely in a defined operating environment.
claims.quote: is a structured argument, supported by evidence, that the Kodiak Driver, the company's autonomous driving system, can operate safely in a defined operating environment
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says it has hauled freight between Dallas and Houston since 2019 with safety drivers in the cab.
claims.quote: Kodiak has delivered freight on the Dallas to Houston route since 2019 with safety drivers in the cab.
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says the company has driven more than 3.5 million autonomous miles since 2019. The release does not say how many of those miles were on the Dallas to Houston route.
claims.quote: Over that time, the company has driven more than 3.5 million autonomous miles.
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak founder and chief executive Don Burnette said the company is on track to finish its preparations and launch driverless highway service by the end of the year.
claims.quote: We are on track to complete our preparations and launch driverless highway service by the end of this year.
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says it began hauling freight with no one in the cab with Atlas Energy Solutions in December 2024, in the Permian Basin of West Texas and eastern New Mexico.
claims.quote: In December 2024, Kodiak became the first company to deploy driverless technology in customer owned-and-operated trucks, when the company began hauling freight with no one in the cab with Atlas Energy Solutions in the Permian Basin of West Texas and Eastern New Mexico.
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says that as of June 30th, 2026 its driving system had been fitted to 35 driverless trucks owned and operated by Atlas.
claims.quote: As of June 30, 2026, the Kodiak Driver had been integrated into 35 driverless trucks owned and operated by Atlas
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says that by June 30th, 2026 the Atlas trucks had passed 40,000 cumulative hours of paid driverless operations.
claims.quote: As of June 30, 2026, the Kodiak Driver had been integrated into 35 driverless trucks owned and operated by Atlas and surpassed 40,000 cumulative hours of paid driverless operations.
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak's release cautions that its forward-looking statements are not predictions of actual performance.
claims.quote: are not predictions of actual performance
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak lists closing its long-haul safety case and launching driverless operations on Texas public highways by the end of 2026 among its forward-looking statements.
claims.quote: Kodiak’s expectations with respect to closing its long-haul safety case and launching driverless operations on public highways in Texas by the end of 2026
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak published its post on IKEA as its driverless launch partner on September 29th, 2026.
claims.quote:
After Four Years of Partnership

September 29, 2026
claims.document: Kodiak post on IKEA as driverless launch partner, September 29th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says IKEA will be its driverless launch shipper partner later in 2026.
claims.quote: IKEA will be Kodiak’s driverless launch shipper partner later in 2026
claims.document: Kodiak post on IKEA as driverless launch partner, September 29th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says it has delivered more than 1,300 loads for IKEA over the last four years.
claims.quote: Over the last four years, Kodiak has delivered more than 1,300 loads
claims.document: Kodiak post on IKEA as driverless launch partner, September 29th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says it has logged more than 750,000 miles autonomously carrying IKEA goods with a safety observer aboard.
claims.quote: logged more than 750,000 miles while autonomously carrying IKEA goods with a safety observer aboard
claims.document: Kodiak post on IKEA as driverless launch partner, September 29th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says the first driver-out leg will run 219 miles, mostly on Interstate 45, between its Houston and Dallas-area facilities.
claims.quote: The initial driver-out leg will cover 219 miles, primarily along Interstate 45 between Kodiak’s Houston and Dallas-area facilities.
claims.document: Kodiak post on IKEA as driverless launch partner, September 29th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak says the leg is part of an established 292-mile delivery route from the IKEA distribution center in Baytown to the IKEA store in Frisco.
claims.quote: part of the established 292-mile delivery route connecting the IKEA distribution center in Baytown with the IKEA store in Frisco
claims.document: Kodiak post on IKEA as driverless launch partner, September 29th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak published its safety case readiness release on September 8th, 2026.
claims.quote:
Safety Case Readiness Reaches 93%

September 8, 2026
claims.document: Kodiak press release on safety case readiness at 93 percent, September 8th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak said on September 8th, 2026 that its readiness measure for long-haul driverless operations reached 93 percent at the end of August. It had been 91 percent at the end of July.
claims.quote: reached 93% at the end of August 2026, up from 91% at the end of July
claims.document: Kodiak press release on safety case readiness at 93 percent, September 8th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak's September 8th, 2026 release says the company reported a readiness measure of 84 percent as of February, 86 percent through April and 91 percent as of July.
claims.quote: The company reported an ARM of 84% as of February, 86% through April and 91% as of July.
claims.document: Kodiak press release on safety case readiness at 93 percent, September 8th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak Director of Safety Frank Fratrik said the confidence to remove the driver is something a program builds.
claims.quote: The confidence to remove the driver is something a program builds
claims.document: Kodiak press release on safety case readiness at 93 percent, September 8th, 2026

claims.text: TxDMV says the 89th Texas Legislature passed Senate Bill 2807 in 2025 and that the bill created a required authorization for commercial operation of automated vehicles on Texas roads.
claims.quote: The 89th Texas Legislature passed Senate Bill 2807 (89R) in 2025 creating a required authorization for the commercial operation of automated vehicles on Texas roads
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: TxDMV says Senate Bill 2807 took effect on September 1st, 2025.
claims.quote: Senate Bill 2807 (89R) became effective September 1, 2025
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: TxDMV says the latest of the rules it and the Texas Department of Public Safety adopted under the law become effective on February 27th, 2026.
claims.quote: The department and DPS both proposed and adopted administrative rules related to the new programs, the latest of which become effective on February 27, 2026
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: TxDMV says the authorization requirements become enforceable 90 days after the final rules take effect. It gives that date as May 28th, 2026.
claims.quote: the authorization requirements become enforceable 90 days after the effect date of the final rules – May 28, 2026
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: TxDMV says every company operating automated vehicles commercially on or after May 28th, 2026 must keep an active TxDMV authorization.
claims.quote: All companies operating automated vehicles commercially on or after May 28, 2026, are required to maintain an active authorization with TxDMV.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: TxDMV says no fee is required for an authorization to operate automated vehicles.
claims.quote: No fees are required for an authorization to operate automated vehicles.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: TxDMV says its automated vehicle authorizations do not expire and stay valid until the department revokes them.
claims.quote: Authorizations do not expire and are valid until revoked by the department.
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: TxDMV says that beginning May 28th, 2026 people can send its Enforcement Division concerns about automated vehicles operating in ways that could result in serious bodily injury or death. The route is txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop.
claims.quote: Beginning May 28, 2026, concerns about automated vehicles operating in ways that could result in serious bodily injury or death can be submitted to the TxDMV Enforcement Division
claims.document: TxDMV Automated Vehicles Regulatory Program page

claims.text: Answering a City of Dallas comment on its adopted automated vehicle rules, TxDMV said the Transportation Code does not allow it to require authorization holders to submit crash history.
claims.quote: Transportation Code, § 545.453 and § 545.456 do not allow the department to
claims.document: TxDMV adopted rules, 43 TAC Chapter 220, Automated Motor Vehicles
claims.note: The agency's answer reads on, across a line break in the PDF text, 'require authorization holders to submit crash history or proof of community stakeholder coordination'. Re-read 2026-10-03 from tmp/src/txdmv_rules.txt lines 318 to 319.

claims.text: Kodiak says it closes its safety case in advance of the driverless highway launch.
claims.quote: the testing and validation required to close its safety case in advance of driverless highway launch
claims.document: Kodiak press release naming the Dallas-Houston launch lane, September 25th, 2026

claims.text: Kodiak founder and chief executive Don Burnette said the company has identified and scheduled the remaining work on its safety case. He said it is concentrated on final engineering verification and validation activities.
claims.quote: We have identified and scheduled the remaining work, which is concentrated on final engineering verification and validation activities.
claims.document: Kodiak AI release on safety case readiness reaching 93 percent, September 8th, 2026

rejected.finding: A safety observer is still aboard the current launch runs
rejected.reason: Neither page says still aboard. The lane page says only that during these end-to-end deliveries the safety observer never touched the wheel (c6), and the IKEA page's with a safety observer aboard describes the four years of IKEA hauling (c22). The present tense framing is dropped.

rejected.finding: More than 3.5 million autonomous miles on the Dallas to Houston route
rejected.reason: The release credits the 3.5 million miles to the company since 2019, not to the route (c12).
